verdicts.quote: “Any integrations that allow other users to grant access to Airtable should use OAuth.”
verdicts.reason: Docs explicitly support OAuth access tokens and recommend OAuth for third‑party integrations, which is the primary method a multi‑tenant agent would use.

verdicts.quote: “Available on all Airtable plans” … “Certain Web API endpoints are only available to our Enterprise Scale customers.”
verdicts.reason: The Web API is available on Free/Team/Business/Enterprise, so developers can self‑serve credentials on a free plan; some endpoints are plan‑gated but access itself is self‑serve.

verdicts.quote: “The following scopes are available to all users:” (lists data.records, data.recordComments, schema.bases, workspacesAndBases, webhook:manage, etc.)
verdicts.reason: The scopes reference spans records CRUD, comments, schema, views/workspaces metadata, and webhooks (plus additional enterprise scopes), indicating a broad API surface.

verdicts.quote: “Airtable's MCP server… The server is available to all users on all plans.”
verdicts.reason: This is Airtable’s own MCP server documentation, confirming it’s official and generally available.

verdicts.quote: “Airtable enforces a rate limit of 5 requests per second (per base)…”; “Monthly limits apply to Free and Team plans only.”
verdicts.reason: The API is buildable now, but rate limits and monthly call caps (and some Enterprise‑only endpoints per docs) are meaningful caveats, so “ready_with_caveats” fits.
